title: The Parliament of Conquerors
setting: A campaign tent large enough for four, pitched on ground none of them recognise. Maps of territory none of them conquered are pinned to the walls. Each man arrived certain he was the largest thing that had ever happened to the world.
stakes: Which of them was right about what an army is for - and whether the one who stopped was the only one who understood.

roles_in_scene.caesar: Conqueror of Gaul, who preferred pardon to proscription because it worked better
roles_in_scene.genghis-khan: Great Khan, who made annihilation a published and perfectly reliable policy
roles_in_scene.napoleon: Emperor of the French, who believes the Code outlives the battles and cannot stop talking about the battles

opening_line: Four men who moved the borders of the world, and no borders left to move.
